featured.label: Human thymus, 3 months (Visium)
featured.why: The loudest adenosine-receptor signal anywhere in the spatial Census: ADORA2A is detected in about 80% of in-tissue spots of this infant thymus. Thymus is ADORA2A's strongest tissue across all 361 human spatial datasets.

featured.label: Human left atrium, donor D6 (Visium)
featured.why: ADORA1 is the cardiac adenosine receptor (it slows the heart). In this donor the atrium detects it in 12% of spots, against 2% in the same donor's ventricle (next section). Same lab, donor and OCT protocol, so the contrast is not a batch artefact between studies.

featured.label: Human left ventricle, donor D6 (Visium)
featured.why: The ventricle partner of the left-atrium section: same donor, same study, same protocol. ADORA1 is detected in about 2% of spots here.

featured.label: Human sinoatrial node, donor AV1, FFPE (Visium)
featured.why: The pacemaker region, where adenosine acting on A1 receptors slows the heart rate. This section has the highest ADORA1 detection of any heart section (37%), but it is one of three FFPE (probe-based) sections from one donor that all read high for ADORA1 and ADORA2A, while the fresh-frozen sinoatrial node sections read 4 to 10%. Treat it as a chemistry contrast as much as an anatomical one.

featured.label: Human rectum, colorectal cancer (Visium)
featured.why: A non-cardiac, non-immune contrast for ADORA2B, the epithelial receptor in the dissociated Census. This rectal cancer section has ADORA2B in 21% of spots, among the highest of any human spatial dataset.

featured.label: Mouse lung, 5 months (Visium)
featured.why: Mouse lung is where Adora2b is most often detected in the spatial Census (about 30% of spots across eight sections). A second organism, and a lung for the A2B-in-airway story.

featured.label: Mouse embryo E9.5, whole section (Slide-seqV2)
featured.why: The closest thing to nervous tissue in the spatial Census: a whole E9.5 embryo with neural tube and early brain, at 10 um bead resolution and with author cell-type labels. It shows what near-absence looks like: all four receptors are detected in under 1% of beads, and the few Adora1 beads sit mostly in the embryonic heart region, not the neural tube.
